items.followUp: Define community level of biological organization.

rubric.why: A population consists of members of one species.
rubric.description: Identifies the organisms as belonging to the same species.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a population contains organisms of the same species.

rubric.why: A population occupies a shared area at a given time.
rubric.description: States that the organisms live in the same area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they live in the same area or habitat.

modelAnswer: A population is a group of organisms of the same species living in the same area at the same time.

items.followUp: Define community level of biological organization.

rubric.why: The control group provides a comparison without the tested treatment.
rubric.description: Describes the control group as not receiving the experimental treatment or change.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the control group.

rubric.why: The experimental group is exposed to the factor being tested.
rubric.description: Describes the experimental group as receiving the treatment or tested factor.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the experimental group.

modelAnswer: The control group is kept under normal conditions and does not receive the treatment being tested.
The experimental group receives the treatment or factor being tested.

rubric.why: Scientific laws are supported by repeated observations or experiments.
rubric.description: Mentions repeated observations or experiments as the basis of a law.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the law is based on repeated scientific evidence.

rubric.why: A law describes a consistent pattern or phenomenon in nature.
rubric.description: States that a scientific law describes a natural phenomenon or pattern.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing what the law states.

modelAnswer: A scientific law is a statement based on repeated observations or experiments that describes a consistent phenomenon or pattern in nature.

items.followUp: State one similarity and one difference between the cell wall and the plasma membrane.

rubric.why: Cell membrane and plasma membrane are generally two names for the same structure.
rubric.description: Recognizes that the terms usually refer to the same cell boundary, rather than two separate membranes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the terms as synonymous or equivalent.

rubric.why: The membrane's selective permeability is a defining feature.
rubric.description: States a key property or function of the membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is selectively permeable or regulates movement of substances.

modelAnswer: Cell membrane and plasma membrane are generally two names for the same boundary around a cell, not two different structures.
This membrane is selectively permeable and controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell.

items.followUp: What is the function of cytoplasm?

rubric.why: Cytoplasm occupies the cell interior, outside the nucleus and within the plasma membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly locating cytoplasm inside the cell, around the nucleus.

rubric.why: Cytoplasm is a semi-fluid material in which organelles are suspended.
rubric.description: Describes its consistency or mentions the organelles it contains.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as jelly-like or semi-fluid, or stating that organelles are suspended in it.

modelAnswer: Cytoplasm is the jelly-like, semi-fluid material inside the cell, between the plasma membrane and the nucleus.

items.followUp: Name any two taxonomic ranks and give one example of an organism classified in each.

rubric.why: A taxon is a group or category used in biological classification.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a taxon as a classification group or category.

rubric.why: Examples demonstrate that taxa include the ranks used in classification.
rubric.description: Names any two valid taxa or taxonomic ranks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming any two ranks, such as kingdom and phylum.

modelAnswer: A taxon is a group or category of organisms at any level of biological classification.
Two taxa are kingdom and phylum.

items.followUp: Write two characteristics of kingdom Plantae.

rubric.why: Fungi have eukaryotic cells with a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying fungi as eukaryotic or having a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Fungi lack chlorophyll and obtain food heterotrophically, commonly by absorption.
rubric.description: Gives a nutritional characteristic of fungi.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that fungi lack chlorophyll, are heterotrophic, or absorb nutrients.

modelAnswer: They lack chlorophyll and obtain their food heterotrophically, usually by absorption.

items.followUp: During which stage of meiosis do chiasmata become visible?

rubric.why: Chiasmata mark sites where crossing over has occurred between homologous chromosomes.
rubric.description: Connects chiasmata with crossing over or genetic-material exchange.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning crossing over or exchange between chromatids.

rubric.why: Chiasmata occur between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they are between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes.

modelAnswer: Chiasmata are the visible points where non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes remain attached after crossing over during meiosis.
